daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The DPR and government have agreed to continue deliberations on the Regional Islands (Daerah Kepulauan) bill until it becomes law. This legislative push comes as parliament advances its priority agenda, while other political dynamics continue to unfold across the executive and oversight institutions.

  • An DPR member stated that military training for Kopdes Merah Putih cooperative manager candidates should continue despite the death of a participant, arguing the program remains necessary.
  • President Prabowo summoned National Police Chief Listyo Sigit to the presidential palace.
  • Vice President Cak Imin said President Prabowo is currently opening a new path for people's economic development.
  • The KPK questioned the former MPR Secretary-General for 10 hours in connection with a gratification case, though the witness remained tight-lipped.
  • Former Ombudsman Chairman Hery Susanto responded to charges that he received Rp 4.8 billion in bribes.
  • The KPK is investigating alleged payments from Denpasar Immigration Office to Silmy Karim, after examining six travel agencies in Bali and finding fees ranging from Rp 100,000 to Rp 2.5 million for foreigner residence permits.
  • The National Police have committed to recruiting persons with disabilities, with selection processes adjusted to match their competencies.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Foreign Ministry is conducting intensive coordination with South Korea to search for two missing Indonesian crew members after a vessel sank in Busan waters. The ministry is working closely with Korean authorities to locate the missing nationals.

  • Indonesia is ready to deploy a rescue team to earthquake-hit Venezuela following the major disaster there.
  • Defence Minister AHY met with Sjafrie at the Defence Ministry for discussions.
  • A former Indonesian ambassador revealed Iran's disappointment with Indonesia's position on certain issues.
  • Indonesia and Switzerland have agreed to cooperate on mineral and metal downstreaming.
  • Army Chief Maruli asked judo athletes to uphold sportsmanship at the KASAD Cup XVI tournament.

Other

Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Bahlil confirmed that supply constraints for medium-rank coal to power plants have been resolved, after earlier expressing surprise that PLN's coal stockpile was nearly depleted in June. The minister is pushing multiple energy diversification initiatives to reduce Indonesia's dependence on imports.

  • Indonesia will phase out diesel imports this year following implementation of the B50 biodiesel mandate.
  • Minister Bahlil is fast-tracking CNG adoption to reduce LPG imports and pushing E20 bioethanol rollout to cut gasoline imports.
  • Indonesia opened a gas plant in Tuban aimed at reducing LPG imports, while the country will adopt Sustainable Aviation Fuel in 2027.
  • Coordinating Minister Airlangga stated that downstreaming has cut ICOR to 3, boosting investment efficiency.
  • Tax official Purbaya conducted a surprise inspection at a Chinese steel plant over alleged underpayment of taxes.
  • Forestry Minister in the UK said Indonesia is committed to building a credible and transparent carbon market.
